features.quote: Beside the Burj I saw a good birket cut in the rock
Near it are a good many cisterns, also cut in the rock.

notes: Own-row 'moat' not recorded (a ditch, not a pool, pit or grave). SWP II p. 30 Burj el Farah (linked in Stage 1b) taken as this unit. Guerin puts the great square tower 'at its eastern extremity' of the ruined hill and the birket 'beside the Burj'; birket coded 'east part' relative to the unit on that two-step reading (hard call: the source locates the birket only by the tower). The cisterns 'near it' have no direction. Spring and Tell el Fera'a passages name no pool, pit or grave; the 'little sanctuary' is not a tomb. SWP says the tower is not older than Saracenic times; this dates the tower, not the birket. Survey entries not accessed.
